title: The Finisher Search: How Lucknow Super Giants Can Identify Genuine Death-Overs Hitters
dek: Genuine finishers are rare. Since 2024, the IPL's best death-overs hitters show what Lucknow Super Giants should look for, and which numbers actually identify one.
excerpt: Lucknow Super Giants have scored slower than the rest of the league at the death since 2024. Boundary rate, more than avoiding dots, separates the genuine finishers.

sections.heading: What Makes a Finisher
body: A finisher's job is to score as fast as possible in the last five overs, often from a standing start. Few players can do it consistently.
Lucknow Super Giants have scored {{ev:fs-t}} an over at the death since 2024, against {{ev:fs-l}} for the rest of the IPL.

body: The chart lists the fastest IPL death hitters since 2024 with at least ninety balls in overs sixteen to twenty. The median among {{ev:fs-n}} qualifiers is {{ev:fs-med}}.
Lucknow Super Giants' fastest qualifier is {{ev:fs-best}}, at {{ev:fs-best-sr}}.

sections.heading: Which Numbers Identify One
body: Among qualifying death hitters, boundary percentage correlates with strike rate at {{ev:fs-r}}, while dot-ball percentage correlates at {{ev:fs-rd}}.

sections.heading: Small Samples at the Death
body: Even the busiest finishers face few balls at the death in a season, so strike rates there swing widely. Two or three seasons of data is the minimum for a judgement.
The small-sample article in this series shows how far short-run numbers regress.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Scout the Boundary Rate
body: Lucknow Super Giants should scout finishers by boundary rate at the death over several seasons, and treat dot-ball avoidance as a secondary skill.
The fastest qualifiers in the chart set the standard to aim for.
